purpose: How an office coffee and water service operator decides which offices inside a drivable route cluster are worth pursuing, estimates what each will actually consume from observed evidence rather than assumed averages, runs the tasting and free-trial play as a costed acquisition instrument, chooses between placing, renting or selling the equipment, and builds a disclosed, honestly sized proposal that displaces self-serve retail buying without overstocking the client or promising a stop the route cannot serve.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is a small independent office coffee and water service that places brewers and water systems in offices and earns recurring revenue from consumables plus a service route

every money quantity in this KB - price, margin, conversion rate, trial cost, account value - is a mechanism the operator computes from their own books and the client's own records, never a market figure quoted from memory

licensing, food-handling, sanitation, potable-water and plumbing obligations vary by jurisdiction and change over time; each is named here as an obligation class the operator must verify with the responsible authority before relying on it
acquisition is bounded by what the route can physically serve; a signed account that cannot be served on the promised cadence is a loss disguised as a win
exclusions: brewer and water-system model selection, physical placement, water-line connection, drainage and sanitation execution - the equipment placement and route setup KB owns all of it
consumables catalog construction, par-level mechanics, stockroom and vehicle inventory, route sequencing and service or cleaning cadence design - owned by the placement and logistics KB

measured stop-level profitability after service begins, consumables repricing, retention programs, stock-out prevention, and expansion into snacks, water upgrades, breakroom supplies or micro-market classes - owned by the route economics and expansion KB

invented specific figures of any kind: no stated market sizes, per-cup prices, margin percentages, trial conversion rates or account-book multiples; every such quantity appears only as a mechanism for computing it from your own records

assertions about what any specific license, food-handling, sanitation, backflow or plumbing rule requires in a named jurisdiction; obligation classes are named and flagged for local verification instead
personalized legal, tax, financial or insurance advice, and the drafting or interpretation of any specific contract
claims about the health effects of tap water, filtration or any beverage, and every fear-based selling tactic built on such claims

competency_questions.question: Which offices in my trade area are worth calling on at all, and in what order should a prospecting day walk them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERRITORY_DEFINITION fixes the drivable clusters and the out-of-cluster rule, OFFICE_SEGMENT_MAP sorts offices by headcount, on-site pattern, culture and tenancy, and PROSPECT_LIST_BUILD produces a cluster-ordered call list with per-row qualification facts

competency_questions.question: How do I estimate what an office will actually drink per week before I have a single day of service history with them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMPTION_POTENTIAL_MODEL states the factor chain and its evidence source per factor and returns a band rather than a single number, and SITE_VISIT_DISCOVERY supplies the observations each factor is drawn from

competency_questions.question: What is this office doing for coffee and water today, and what does that tell me about whether it can be won and how?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCUMBENT_SUPPLY_DIAGNOSIS classifies the current supply mode, records the incumbent failure signature that makes the account winnable, and requires an existing-agreement check before anything is placed

competency_questions.question: How do I build an honest comparison against an office that sends an employee to a club store, without inventing savings?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISPLACEMENT_ECONOMICS gives the comparison structure, requires every line to come from the client's own receipts, hours and outage stories, and states the rule for conceding when the client's own arithmetic wins

competency_questions.question: Who feels the pain, who controls the recurring budget, who can veto on space or plumbing grounds, and how do I reach them without being the vendor everyone avoids?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DECISION_MAKER_MAP separates pain-holder, budget-holder and veto-holder including the landlord in leased suites, and OUTREACH_SEQUENCE describes permission-based contact with identification up front and an easy opt-out

competency_questions.question: Should this account get a placed brewer, a rented one, or should the client buy the equipment outright, and how is the hardware cost actually recovered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLACEMENT_MODEL_SELECTION describes all three models, names where the equipment cost is recovered in each, and gives the fit rule by consumption band and expected account life together with the duty to disclose the recovery rather than call the machine free

competency_questions.question: Is a tasting or a free trial worth running for this prospect, and what does that trial actually cost me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TASTING_TRIAL_PLAY describes the structured play with a champion and a decision date, and TRIAL_ECONOMICS_MECHANISM decomposes trial cost into equipment days, product consumed and route visits and frames payback against a conversion rate the operator must measure from logged trials

competency_questions.question: What must the trial agreement say so that nobody is surprised on the last day?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRIAL_TERMS_AND_EXIT requires a written end date, equipment ownership and retrieval, product responsibility and an explicit no-automatic-billing rule, and DISCLOSURE_FIRST_SELLING makes affirmative opt-in the conduct standard

competency_questions.question: How big should the first order and the standing order be so the client is not overstocked into resentment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_CONSUMPTION_PROPOSAL sizes opening quantities at or below the low case of the consumption band with a narrow opening variety and a scheduled true-up, and PROPOSAL_CONSTRUCTION shows the assumption and the review point in the document the client signs

competency_questions.question: Can this account carry a recurring route stop, and how do I decline the ones that cannot without guessing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_QUALIFICATION_GATE screens the low case of the consumption band against the mechanism by which a stop must repay its service and drive time, lists the non-economic disqualifiers, and requires a written decline reason with a reconsideration condition

competency_questions.question: Which permit, food-handling, sanitation, water and vendor-insurance obligation classes touch me before I can put equipment in someone else's breakroom?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANCE_CLASS_SCREEN enumerates obligations as classes with the authority likely to own each and the instruction to verify current rules in your jurisdiction, and WATER_SERVICE_FIT_SCREEN converts the water-related classes plus landlord consent into a pre-sale feasibility verdict

competency_questions.question: Which agreement terms must I be able to explain in plain language before I ask an office manager for a signature?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGREEMENT_TERMS_LITERACY names the term classes (initial term and renewal behaviour, minimums, equipment ownership and removal, price-change, service commitments, assignment) and states that drafting and interpretation belong to qualified counsel and that the prospect should have their own advisor read it

competency_questions.question: How do I answer we already buy it ourselves, our landlord provides it, or we tried a service and they were unreliable, without disparaging anyone or selling on fear?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OBJECTION_AND_RISK_HANDLING gives an evidence-based response to each of the four common objections and DISCLOSURE_FIRST_SELLING forbids water-quality, hygiene or morale fear claims as closing devices

competency_questions.question: How do I tell whether my acquisition effort is actually producing new stops, and what must a signed account carry when it leaves acquisition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PIPELINE_CADENCE_AND_FORECAST counts qualified prospects, visits, live trials with decision dates and outstanding proposals and forecasts stops from the operator's own observed step rates, and ACCOUNT_HANDOFF_PACKET lists every verified fact the placement and route side needs on install day

glossary.definition: The trade of supplying workplaces with brewing equipment and the coffee, tea, cups, creamer, filters and related consumables that feed it, delivered on a recurring service route rather than sold over a counter.

Putting a brewer or water system into a client site on loan, where title stays with the operator and the hardware cost is recovered over time inside the consumables margin; the arrangement is only sound when the account's consumption and expected life plausibly cover that recovery, and the recovery must be disclosed rather than described as free equipment.

The recurring product an account draws down between visits - coffee in whatever format the placed equipment takes, tea, creamer and sweetener, cups, lids, stirrers, filters and water - which is where the recurring revenue of an office coffee account actually lives.

The low-to-high range of expected product draw for a prospect, produced by multiplying observed factors rather than quoting an average; the low end is the number every commitment decision in this KB is made against.

The fraction of an office's total beverage demand that your placed equipment will actually serve, after allowing for people who bring a thermos from home, walk to a café, or drink only what they buy themselves; the factor most often set to one by optimistic estimators and the most common cause of an over-sized opening order.

A water dispenser plumbed into the building's cold-water supply with filtration, as opposed to a cooler fed by delivered bottles; it removes bottle handling from the route but requires an accessible line, sometimes drainage, landlord permission, and trade and permit classes that must be verified locally.

The status quo in most unserved offices: an employee buys coffee and supplies at a club store, warehouse retailer or online and expenses them, so the office believes it pays only the shelf price and does not count the buying trips, stocking labour, stock-outs and dead home-grade equipment that the displacement comparison surfaces.

One serviced account as the route sees it - a physical visit consuming drive time, in-building time and service time - and therefore the true unit that acquisition must qualify against, since revenue accrues per account but cost accrues per visit.

The person inside the account who feels the pain of an empty pot, gathers colleague reactions during a tasting, and will tell you when something is wrong; usually an office manager or admin, rarely the person who signs, and the single most fragile dependency in a young account.

A document evidencing the operator's insurance coverage that many client organisations require from any vendor entering their premises, often with named-insured or coverage-class conditions set by the client's own risk policy; treated here as a vendor requirement class to confirm with each prospect, not as a legal or insurance recommendation.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for ocs_market_targeting_and_account_acquisition work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix the geographic envelope you will sell into before a single prospect is called, because in office coffee the unit that carries cost is the route stop and a signed account outside your drive cluster consumes more windshield time than its consumables can ever pay for. The territory is drawn as a small number of dense clusters - office parks, medical and professional corridors, industrial-park front offices, downtown multi-tenant buildings - chosen so that a day of service can be walked as one tight loop, and each cluster is recorded with a counted number of candidate offices so you know whether it can feed the route at all. The definition also carries an explicit rule for the attractive prospect that falls outside every cluster: decline it, waitlist it against future density in that corridor, or accept it as a documented density exception with the extra drive time acknowledged rather than pretended away.

included: drive-loop feasibility of a service day
excluded: route sequencing, vehicle loading and stop order
measured stop-level profitability once service is running
hiring or vehicle capacity planning

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a week of actual drive-time logs from real service runs contradicts the assumed one-day loop for a cluster

pros.claim: Clustering before prospecting prevents the classic first-year mistake of an account book scattered across a county that no single day can serve
pros.example: declining a forty-person office twenty-five minutes past the last stop until two more prospects in that corridor sign

pros.claim: A counted candidate inventory tells you early whether a corridor can ever carry a route day, before you have spent months prospecting it
pros.example: finding that a light-industrial park holds only four front offices with more than a handful of staff

cons.claim: A tight cluster caps the addressable prospect count and can stall growth when the chosen corridors are already served by an incumbent
cons.example: three business parks whose largest tenants all sit under a competitor's multi-year agreement

failure_modes: drawing the territory around where the operator lives rather than where office density actually is
accepting one prestige account far outside the cluster and rebuilding the whole run around it
counting buildings instead of occupied suites, so the candidate inventory is fiction
acceptance_tests: each named cluster can be driven as a single service loop within a working day and carries a counted list of candidate offices
a written rule exists for what happens to an out-of-cluster prospect, and any exception granted is recorded with the extra drive time it adds
revisit_triggers: a cluster's qualified candidate list is exhausted
an anchor account that justified a cluster is lost
a new office park, medical building or business campus opens in the trade area

nodes.definition: Sort the offices inside the territory into segments that predict both consumption and buying behaviour, because a hundred badges tells you almost nothing on its own. The segmenting facts are headcount band, on-site density (fully on-site, hybrid with named in-office days, or a field-based crew that touches the office weekly), workplace culture (a law or design firm where people drink espresso through the afternoon behaves nothing like a warehouse front office that runs one drip pot), tenancy (a single-tenant suite with its own kitchen versus a multi-tenant floor with a shared or landlord-run breakroom), and shift pattern (a single day shift versus a round-the-clock operation whose night crew quietly doubles the pot count). Segment membership is what tells you which equipment class to propose, which acquisition motion to use, and roughly how much error to expect in the first consumption estimate - and it is the first thing real service data revises.

included: on-site day patterns and hybrid schedules
tenancy type and who controls the breakroom
excluded: which specific brewer or water unit suits a segment
pricing by segment
service cadence design per segment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: first-cycle draw data from won accounts in a segment differs systematically from what the segment predicted

pros.claim: Segmenting by on-site days rather than headcount alone stops the systematic over-forecasting of hybrid offices
pros.example: a sixty-badge firm with a three-day in-office policy that behaves like a much smaller account every Friday

cons.claim: Segments built from directory and public headcount data are frequently wrong until a site visit corrects them
cons.example: a listed staff count that silently includes field technicians who enter the building twice a month

cons.claim: Culture signals are soft and easy to over-read from a lobby impression
cons.example: assuming a design studio is an espresso account when the team actually drinks canned energy drinks

failure_modes: treating headcount as a proxy for consumption in a hybrid workplace
ignoring multi-tenant buildings where the landlord already supplies the shared breakroom
missing a second or third shift that is invisible during a daytime visit
acceptance_tests: every segment is defined by facts an operator can observe or verify rather than by an impression, and each prospect row carries its segment and the evidence that placed it there
revisit_triggers: actual service data from won accounts contradicts a segment's expected draw
a large employer in the territory changes its in-office policy
a segment produces repeated losses at the same objection

nodes.definition: Assemble the working call list from sources that actually reveal where offices sit and how many people occupy them - lobby tenant directories in multi-tenant buildings, business-park monument signage, property-manager rosters, chamber and trade-association listings, public licensing and permit rosters, and your own windshield observation of parking-lot fill at ten in the morning - then order it by cluster first and segment second so a prospecting day walks a building rather than crossing a county. Each row carries only the facts that decide whether a visit is warranted: address and suite, estimated headcount and its source, tenancy type, any competitor equipment or delivery seen, and the date the row was last touched. The list is a live artefact whose rows die quickly, so it carries a staleness date rather than pretending to be a database.

included: source assembly for office locations and occupancy
per-row qualification facts and staleness dating
excluded: the territory decision itself
decision-maker identification inside a prospect
purchasing lead lists whose provenance and consent status cannot be checked

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a prospecting week shows a high share of rows that no longer exist at the listed suite

pros.claim: A cluster-ordered list converts a prospecting day into a walk of one building instead of a drive across the trade area
pros.example: eleven suites in a single three-storey professional building visited in one morning

cons.claim: Directory headcounts and lobby boards go stale fast, so a meaningful share of rows are dead on arrival
cons.example: a suite still listed to a firm that downsized into a shared workspace two years earlier

failure_modes: building a large list of unqualified rows and calling it a pipeline
collecting contact data from sources whose terms or consent status the operator has not checked
letting the list age without a staleness date so the same dead suites are visited twice
acceptance_tests: every row carries an address with suite, a headcount estimate with its source, a tenancy type and a date, and rows are grouped by cluster before any calling begins
revisit_triggers: a building changes tenants or a major tenant vacates
a cluster's rows are more than a season old

nodes.definition: For each live prospect, separate three roles that are rarely the same person. The pain-holder is whoever currently runs out to buy coffee, hears the complaints and finds the pot empty before a client meeting - usually an office manager or an admin, and the person your tasting must delight. The budget-holder approves a recurring line item and may be an owner, a controller, a practice administrator or facilities, and a proposal that never reaches them dies quietly. The veto-holder can stop the deal on grounds that have nothing to do with coffee: facilities over counter space or an electrical circuit, information technology over a network-connected machine, and in a leased suite the landlord or property manager whose rules may govern breakroom equipment, plumbing penetrations and deliveries entirely. The map records who feels it, who signs it, who must simply be told, and what the building's rules say.

included: landlord and property-manager authority in leased suites
excluded: gathering personal information about individuals beyond their business role and business contact details
negotiating the client's internal politics on their behalf

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a lost deal post-mortem shows the proposal never reached the person who could approve recurring spend

pros.claim: Selling to the pain-holder while confirming the budget-holder early avoids a proposal that dies unopened in someone else's inbox
pros.example: an office manager who loves the tasting but has no authority over recurring spend above a limit the controller sets

cons.claim: Mapping too broadly turns a simple counter-top decision into a committee and slows the close for no gain
cons.example: looping facilities into a plug-in brewer that needs nothing but a spare outlet

failure_modes: presenting to an enthusiastic champion with no budget authority and calling it a live deal
discovering the landlord controls the breakroom only after the proposal is signed
letting the whole account rest on one champion with no second contact recorded
acceptance_tests: the three roles are named for the account, with a note on the building's rules for tenant breakroom equipment, before any proposal is presented
at least one alternate contact inside the account is recorded alongside the champion
revisit_triggers: the champion leaves or changes role
the account changes landlord, moves suite, or is acquired

nodes.definition: The contact motion that actually produces office coffee appointments: a low-pressure in-person drop with a sample and a card in a building you already service, a referral ask from an existing stop or a property manager who trusts your van showing up on time, and a short call or message follow-up that states plainly who you are, that you sell coffee and water service, why you are contacting this office, and how to be left alone. The sequence is shaped by two realities of this trade - the pain-holder is interruptible only at certain hours, and a breakroom is semi-private space you enter by invitation rather than by walking past a receptionist into someone's kitchen. Contact volume is capped by the route day, so the sequence prioritises buildings you are already inside over cold corridors.

included: in-person sampling drops in serviced buildings
referral asks from existing stops and property managers
contact cadence bounded by route hours
excluded: pressure tactics, manufactured urgency and repeat contact after a request to stop
entering restricted or no-solicitation premises against posted policy
outreach to consumers at home

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged outcomes by contact channel show one motion producing appointments at a materially different rate than assumed

pros.claim: Physical sampling inside buildings you already serve converts far better than cold calling because the prospect can watch your service van arrive on schedule and ask the neighbouring tenant about you
pros.example: the suite next door to an existing stop asking what the weekly deliveries are

cons.claim: Drop-in prospecting burns route hours and irritates receptionists in buildings with no-solicitation policies
cons.example: a lobby that posts a no-soliciting rule the operator only notices on the second visit

failure_modes: pitching whoever is at the front desk instead of reaching the mapped roles
continuing to contact a prospect who has asked to be left alone
letting prospecting drops eat the service window so existing stops are served late
acceptance_tests: every first contact identifies the operator, the company and the reason for contact, and records an opt-out request permanently against the prospect row
prospecting hours are scheduled outside the committed service window for existing accounts
revisit_triggers: response rates in a cluster fall off sharply
a building or property manager sets new vendor access rules

nodes.definition: The structured breakroom walk that replaces guessed consumption with observed evidence, and the single highest-yield hour in the whole acquisition process because every downstream number rests on it. You count the people actually present and ask how many are in on a typical day versus a Friday; you read the counter (a home-style drip maker, a competitor brewer with a service sticker, a stack of club-store bags, a pod carousel); you read the bins for cup, bottle and grounds volume; you find the water source and whether there is an accessible cold line under the sink, a floor drain, or only a delivered cooler; you measure counter run, outlet positions and the closet or shelf that would hold stock; you note delivery access - hours, dock, elevator, badge or escort rules - and you ask the one question that reveals everything: when does the pot run dry. The visit produces a dated audit sheet, not an impression.

excluded: installation design, line routing and equipment specification
sanitation remediation work
photographing people or capturing anything the client has not agreed to

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: install-day surprises (access, space, water, occupancy) traced back to fields the audit sheet did not capture

pros.claim: A counter-and-bin audit produces a consumption estimate grounded in what is actually consumed rather than what a headcount implies
pros.example: an empty two-pound bag and a bin of single-serve cups on a Wednesday afternoon in an office that claims light coffee use

pros.claim: Capturing access facts during discovery removes the most common first-delivery failure before it can happen
pros.example: learning that the freight elevator needs booking a day ahead and that deliveries are refused after mid-morning

cons.claim: The visit consumes prospecting time and can only happen when the pain-holder is free, so it throttles pipeline throughput
cons.example: three attempts to catch an office manager who is always out at lunch when the route passes

failure_modes: touring the office and writing nothing down, so the proposal is built from memory
asking headcount and never asking how many people are physically in on a typical day
missing the second shift, the adjoining suite of the same tenant, or the kitchen on another floor
acceptance_tests: the audit sheet is dated and records occupancy, current equipment and product, bin evidence, water source, storage and counter space, and delivery access rules
each consumption factor later used in the estimate can be traced to a line on this sheet
revisit_triggers: the account moves, expands into another suite, or changes its in-office schedule
the audit sheet is older than a season when the proposal is finally presented

nodes.definition: Classify how this office gets coffee and water today, because each mode has a different winnable path, a different objection and a different risk. The modes are: self-serve retail buying, where an employee expenses club-store or online purchases; an incumbent office coffee service under agreement with placed equipment; landlord- or building-provided service in a shared breakroom; an employee-funded arrangement where people bring their own or run a kitty; a single-serve pod habit bought online; and genuinely nothing at all. The diagnosis also records the incumbent's failure signature - late or missed deliveries, a machine broken for weeks, product nobody likes, an invoice that keeps changing - because that signature, not price, is usually what makes an account winnable. Where an agreement may exist, the diagnosis stops and asks the client to check their own obligations with their own advisor; you never counsel anyone to break a contract they signed.

included: existing-agreement check before anything is placed
excluded: disparaging a competitor or making claims about their product or conduct you cannot evidence
advising a client on the meaning or enforceability of their existing agreement
price-war tactics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a signed account where an undisclosed incumbent agreement surfaced after commitment

pros.claim: Knowing the supply mode selects the argument: convenience and hidden labour for self-serve buyers, reliability for a failing incumbent, permission and access for a landlord-served suite
pros.example: a brewer under an incumbent's agreement that has been broken for weeks with no service visit

cons.claim: Prospects routinely misreport their arrangement, and a forgotten agreement can surface after you have already committed equipment
cons.example: an office manager who does not know a predecessor signed a multi-year service agreement with an automatic renewal

failure_modes: taking the client's word that there is no agreement and placing equipment on that basis
attacking the incumbent instead of documenting the gap the client already describes
missing that the building, not the tenant, controls and pays for the breakroom
acceptance_tests: the account's supply mode is recorded with the evidence that established it, and any possible existing agreement is flagged with a request that the client confirm their own position before a start date is set
revisit_triggers: the incumbent replaces equipment or repairs the failure that opened the door
the building changes what it provides in shared breakrooms

nodes.definition: Build the account's expected draw as an explicit chain of observable quantities rather than a quoted figure: people physically on site on a typical day, times the share of them who drink the product at all, times cups per drinker per day for that culture, times the days per week the office is occupied, times the capture share you will realistically serve after allowing for thermoses from home and the café downstairs - then converted into product units per period using the yield of the brewing format you intend to place, since a bean, a fractional pack and a single-serve cup produce completely different unit counts from the same cup demand. Every factor comes from the site-visit sheet or from a record the client supplies, each is written down as a stated assumption, and the output is a band with an explicit low case. No factor in this chain may be a market average you half-remember; where you have no evidence for a factor, you widen the band rather than invent a number.

included: the factor chain and its evidence source per factor
an explicit low-mid-high band with stated assumptions
excluded: pricing the consumption or computing margin
par-level and order-quantity mechanics for the stockroom
post-service consumption analytics for repricing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the first two service cycles of measured product draw for this account, compared against the predicted band

pros.claim: An explicit factor chain makes the estimate auditable, so a wrong assumption is corrected in one place instead of invalidating the whole proposal
pros.example: halving the capture share for an office whose ground floor holds a busy café and leaving every other factor intact

cons.claim: Multiplying five uncertain factors produces a band wide enough to look unimpressive to a client who wants one confident number
cons.example: a range whose low end will not carry a stop while its high end easily would

cons.claim: Format conversion errors are silent and large, because the same cup demand maps to very different unit counts across bean, fractional pack and single-serve formats
cons.example: quoting a standing order in packs after estimating demand in cups without converting yield

failure_modes: setting capture share to one because everyone in the office said they drink coffee
using badge count instead of typical on-site attendance in a hybrid office
presenting only the optimistic end of the band to make the proposal look better
borrowing a per-person consumption figure from an unverified source and treating it as fact
acceptance_tests: each factor is traceable to a site-visit observation or a client-supplied record rather than to an assumed industry average
the estimate is stated as a band whose low case is the one used for every commitment decision downstream
the cup-to-unit conversion names the brewing format it assumes
revisit_triggers: the first full service cycles of actual draw fall outside the estimated band
the account changes headcount, in-office schedule or shift pattern
the placed format changes, invalidating the yield conversion

nodes.definition: Decide, before anything is promised, which water offering is even possible at this site. A delivered-bottle cooler needs floor space, a delivery path and somewhere to stage empties; a point-of-use plumbed system needs an accessible cold-water line, a shutoff, sometimes drainage, almost always the landlord's written permission in a leased suite, and it touches trade and permit classes - plumbing work, backflow or cross-connection requirement classes, potable-water handling - that vary by jurisdiction and must be verified locally with the responsible authority before you rely on any of them. The screen produces a plain feasibility verdict plus the list of conditions that would have to be true (landlord consent, a licensed trade, a permit class confirmed), so that no proposal ever contains a water option the building will not allow or the operator is not permitted to install.

included: trade and permit obligation classes to verify locally
excluded: the actual installation, line routing, filter selection and sanitising procedure
asserting what any specific plumbing, backflow or water rule requires
claims about water quality or health effects

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a water option sold and then withdrawn because a landlord, trade or permit condition turned out to be unmet

pros.claim: Screening water feasibility before the proposal prevents promising a plumbed system that a landlord will never approve
pros.example: a suite whose lease forbids penetrations into base-building plumbing without written consent

cons.claim: The screen introduces a question the prospect often cannot answer, stalling the proposal until a property manager replies
cons.example: a week lost waiting for building management to confirm whether under-sink work is permitted

failure_modes: offering a plumbed system on the assumption that a sink implies an accessible and permitted connection point
treating a verbal landlord approval as sufficient in a building that requires written consent
presenting filtration with an implied health claim rather than as a taste and convenience choice
acceptance_tests: the proposal contains only water options this site's verdict marks feasible, and every condition (consent, trade, permit class) is listed with an owner and a verify-locally flag
no water option is described with a health or safety claim the operator cannot support from a verifiable published source
revisit_triggers: the account moves suite or the building changes its rules on tenant plumbing work
a jurisdiction updates the trade or permit classes touching point-of-use installations

nodes.definition: Enumerate, as classes rather than as specific rules, every obligation that attaches to putting food and beverage equipment into other people's workplaces and servicing it from a vehicle: business registration and local licensing classes; food-handling and sanitation requirement classes that may cover handling coffee, tea, dairy and creamer and cleaning brewing equipment; potable-water, cross-connection and backflow requirement classes for plumbed systems; product transport and storage requirement classes for a route vehicle; and the vendor-side requirements the client's own organisation imposes, which in practice bite sooner than anything else - a certificate of insurance with conditions set by their risk policy, badging or background-check requirements, a vendor-onboarding portal, or a purchasing process with its own paperwork. Each class is recorded with the authority or party likely to own it and an explicit instruction to verify current rules in your jurisdiction before relying on it. This KB never states what a specific rule requires and is not legal advice.

included: obligation classes with likely owning authority
a verify-locally instruction attached to every class
the timing at which each must be satisfied
excluded: executing sanitation and cleaning procedures on route
stating what any named jurisdiction actually requires
legal, tax or insurance advice of any kind

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a verification call to a local authority or a client's procurement team returns a requirement the class register did not anticipate

pros.claim: Screening obligation classes before proposing stops the deal that signs and then stalls in a vendor portal or on a permit question
pros.example: a corporate prospect whose onboarding requires an insurance certificate with conditions the operator must arrange before a first delivery date can be set

cons.claim: Class-level treatment cannot tell an operator what they actually must do, so real verification work still has to be done per jurisdiction and per client
cons.example: two neighbouring municipalities in the same trade area handling food-adjacent service registration differently

failure_modes: assuming that because coffee is not cooked, no food-handling or sanitation class applies anywhere in the trade area
treating a rule learned in one jurisdiction as settled across the whole territory
discovering a client's insurance or badging requirement on install day
acceptance_tests: every obligation is written as a class with the authority or party to check and a verify-locally flag, and none is stated as a settled requirement
the vendor-requirement checklist for each target segment is confirmed with the prospect before the proposal is presented
revisit_triggers: the operator expands into a new municipality or county
a client segment introduces new vendor onboarding or insurance conditions
an authority publishes a change touching food-adjacent service or potable water

nodes.definition: Construct the honest comparison against the status quo in which somebody drives to a club store: the client's real out-of-pocket on product at retail, plus the labour cost of the employee hours spent buying, hauling, stocking and cleaning, plus the cost of running out (the mid-morning coffee run three people take, the meeting with nothing to serve, the pot somebody has to make), plus the home-grade equipment they quietly replace every so often - all set against your all-in recurring service cost. The discipline that makes this node honest is that every line comes from the client's own receipts, their own stated hourly cost and their own outage stories; you supply the structure of the comparison and your own price, and nothing else. Where the arithmetic shows the client is genuinely cheaper on product alone, you say so and let the decision rest on convenience, consistency and freed-up staff time rather than a savings claim you cannot support.

included: explicit statement of where your service costs more
excluded: invented savings percentages or generic industry cost claims
competitor price attacks
repricing an account once it is running

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client challenges a comparison line and the source cannot be produced from their own records

pros.claim: A comparison built from the client's own receipts survives a controller's scrutiny in a way that a generic savings claim never does
pros.example: a client who pulls three months of club-store receipts and discovers the buying trips cost more than the coffee

cons.claim: Honest arithmetic sometimes shows the client is cheaper as they are, and the operator must concede it and sell on service or walk away
cons.example: a four-person suite whose quarterly bag of coffee costs less than any serviced arrangement could

cons.claim: Quantifying the client's internal labour requires numbers only they can give, so the comparison stalls without their participation
cons.example: an office manager unwilling to put an hourly figure on their own time spent shopping

failure_modes: assigning a labour rate the client never stated in order to make the case close
counting the same hidden cost twice across categories
presenting the comparison as a guaranteed saving rather than as a structure filled with the client's own inputs
acceptance_tests: every line in the comparison names its source as a client receipt, a client-stated rate, a client-reported outage, or the operator's own quoted price
the comparison shows the categories where the service costs more, not only where it costs less
revisit_triggers: retail product prices or the operator's own cost base shift materially
the client's staffing or in-office pattern changes the labour side of the comparison

nodes.definition: The explicit go or no-go that decides whether a prospect becomes a proposal at all, applied before a trial machine or a placement is committed. The economic leg compares the low case of the consumption band against the mechanism by which a stop must pay for itself: the gross margin the account generates between visits has to cover the service time and drive time that visit consumes, and any placed hardware has to be recoverable over a plausible account life. That mechanism is computed with the operator's own cost of time and their own product margins - this KB supplies the structure, never a threshold figure. The gate also has non-economic legs that fail an account outright: no reachable budget-holder, an unresolved incumbent agreement, a site condition or access rule you cannot serve, or a vendor requirement you cannot meet. A documented density exception is allowed when the prospect sits inside a building you already visit, because the marginal drive time is near zero. Declining early is the cheapest thing this KB does.

included: low-case screening against a stated mechanism
written decline reason and reconsideration condition
excluded: measured stop-level profitability once the account is running
route insertion and sequencing decisions
any fixed dollar threshold presented as an industry standard

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured service and drive time from the running route shows the assumed cost per visit is wrong for a cluster

pros.claim: Declining sub-scale accounts early protects the route from stops that consume more service time than their consumables can ever generate
pros.example: a six-person suite that wants a full brewer programme and a weekly visit in a building you do not otherwise serve

pros.claim: A written decline reason turns a rejection into a future lead instead of a forgotten name
pros.example: a prospect declined for density that is revisited the week a second tenant in the same building signs

cons.claim: A strict gate rejects small accounts that would have anchored a building and pulled in its neighbours
cons.example: a small tenant in a professional building with eight other suites you have not yet won

failure_modes: screening against the optimistic end of the consumption band because the deal is wanted
applying the gate after equipment has already been promised or trialled
granting density exceptions so freely that the exception becomes the rule
acceptance_tests: the gate is applied to the low case of the consumption band, and the decision is recorded before any equipment is committed
every declined prospect carries a written reason and the condition under which it would be reconsidered
each granted density exception names the building and the existing stop that justifies it
revisit_triggers: a cluster gains or loses an anchor stop, changing marginal drive time for its neighbours
the operator's own cost of service time or product margin changes materially
declined prospects in a segment are later won profitably by a competitor

nodes.definition: The conduct rule that governs every other node here. Identify yourself, your company and the fact that you sell coffee and water service at first contact. Present the total recurring cost as the client will experience it, the equipment obligation attached to it, and the exit terms before you ask for a signature rather than after the first invoice raises questions. Never manufacture fear about tap water, hygiene or employee retention to move a sale - a taste and convenience argument is honest, a health scare is not, and any claim you cannot support from a verifiable published source does not get made. Never exploit an office manager's unfamiliarity with recurring-service contracts by rushing a signature or discouraging review. Extend particular care where the buyer is a sole proprietor, a small nonprofit or a first-time office manager with no procurement support: when the honest answer is that the prospect is better off buying their own bags for now, say so plainly and leave the door open.

included: cost, obligation and exit disclosure before signature
prohibition on fear-based water, hygiene and morale claims
extra care with unsophisticated or resource-constrained buyers
the duty to advise against buying when that is the honest answer
excluded: any assertion about health effects of water or beverages
personalised legal, financial or insurance advice
drafting the client's internal policies

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a post-signature complaint or cancellation traced to something the client says was not disclosed before signing

pros.claim: Disclosure-first selling produces accounts that do not churn in month three when the first full invoice arrives
pros.example: an office manager who already knew the minimum order and the equipment tie before signing and is not surprised by either

pros.claim: Refusing fear-based water claims protects the operator from a claim they cannot substantiate and from the reputational damage when a client checks
pros.example: declining to imply that a building's tap water is unsafe and selling the taste and convenience of filtration instead

cons.claim: Full disclosure of the equipment obligation loses deals a vaguer pitch would have closed
cons.example: a prospect who walks once told the placed brewer stays tied to continuing product purchases

failure_modes: describing placed equipment as free without disclosing that its cost is recovered in product pricing
leaving the minimum, the renewal behaviour or the removal cost to be discovered later
using an anecdote about mould or contamination as a closing device
pushing a full programme onto a buyer whose own numbers do not support it
acceptance_tests: before signature the prospect can restate the recurring cost, the equipment obligation and how the agreement ends
no sales material or verbal claim about health, safety or water quality is used that the operator cannot support with a verifiable published source
at least one honest downgrade or decline recommendation is on record where the client's own numbers did not support the programme
revisit_triggers: a client reports being surprised by a cost or obligation after signing
a new product or water line introduces claims that need substantiation review

nodes.definition: Choose how the equipment gets onto the counter, because the three models put the risk in completely different places. Under placement the brewer or dispenser stays yours and its cost is recovered inside the consumables margin across the account's life, which is why placement demands a consumption floor, a plausible account life and an appetite for financing hardware into a stop you might lose. Under rental the client pays a stated recurring equipment charge, so the recovery is explicit and visible instead of buried in product pricing, which suits a client who wants to see what they are paying for. Under purchase the client owns the machine outright and you sell only product and service, which fits a strong-volume account that dislikes any tie and shifts service-and-repair expectations onto a different footing. The selection is made from the consumption band, the expected account life, the client's own preference between capital and operating spend, and your own equipment inventory position - and whichever model is chosen, the recovery mechanism is disclosed rather than hidden behind the word free.

included: the three commercial models and where each recovers hardware cost
fit rules by consumption band and expected account life
excluded: which brewer or water unit model to install and its specification
installation and commissioning work
long-run margin measurement and repricing of the account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recovered-versus-written-off outcomes on past placements, measured from the operator's own equipment history

pros.claim: Matching the model to the consumption band keeps hardware capital tied only to accounts that can plausibly repay it
pros.example: offering rental rather than placement to a modest-volume office that wants a premium machine

cons.claim: Placement is the easiest model to sell and the easiest to regret, because the capital is gone before the account has proven it will stay
cons.example: a machine placed in a startup suite that vacates the building within the year

cons.claim: A purchase model removes the recurring equipment tie that makes consumables revenue sticky
cons.example: a client who buys the machine outright and later sources product elsewhere

failure_modes: placing premium equipment to win a deal the consumption band cannot support
calling placed equipment free while pricing the recovery into product without saying so
ignoring removal and refurbishment cost when a placement ends early
acceptance_tests: the chosen model names where hardware cost is recovered and the consumption and account-life assumptions that make that recovery plausible
the client is told in plain words how the equipment is paid for under the model proposed
revisit_triggers: actual draw settles well below the band that justified a placement
equipment inventory tightens so placements must be rationed
an account signals an imminent move or downsizing

nodes.definition: Size the opening order, the standing quantity and the product breadth to what the account will actually drink, and build the correction step into the offer instead of inflating the start. In practice: set opening quantities at or below the low case of the consumption band; keep the initial variety narrow enough that nothing sits long enough to go stale; propose no minimum-volume commitment the client's own numbers do not support; and schedule an explicit review after the first cycles at which quantities move up or down from observed draw, with the client told at signing that the first order is deliberately conservative and will be adjusted. Overstocking is the fastest way to convert a delighted new account into a resentful one that opens a closet full of product nobody ordered and cancels at the first opportunity - and it is the specific harm this business must not cause, whatever it does to a month's revenue.

included: a scheduled true-up the client agrees to at signing
excluded: par-level mechanics, stockroom layout and van inventory design
ongoing repricing and margin management
stock-out prevention programmes on a running account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: first-cycle draw for new accounts compared against their opening order quantities across a season

pros.claim: Opening light and topping up builds trust and produces an accurate standing quantity from real draw within a couple of cycles
pros.example: an office that asks for more of one blend and drops another entirely after the first month

pros.claim: Refusing an unsupported minimum removes the single most common source of first-year resentment and cancellation
pros.example: declining to write a monthly minimum a twelve-person hybrid office could only meet by wasting product

cons.claim: Opening conservatively risks an early stock-out, which is the one failure a new account remembers longest
cons.example: running dry in the second week before the first scheduled review

failure_modes: sizing the opening order from the optimistic end of the band because it looks better on paper
loading a new account with wide variety that ages out before it is drunk
letting the scheduled review slip so an over- or under-sized standing order becomes permanent
using a minimum commitment as a substitute for qualifying the account properly
acceptance_tests: the opening order quantity is at or below the low case of the consumption band and the review point is written into what the client signs
no proposed minimum-purchase commitment exceeds the low case of the estimated consumption
opening variety is limited to items the account's own tasting or current purchases evidence
revisit_triggers: observed draw in the first cycles differs materially from the opening assumption
the account reports product ageing on the shelf or repeated stock-outs
the account's headcount or in-office schedule changes

nodes.definition: Assemble the document the prospect actually decides on, and make it checkable. It states the consumption assumption in the open with its evidence and its band; the equipment model and exactly what it obligates; the product list with specific items and formats rather than categories; the service cadence you are committing to and what happens when you miss it; the water option if any, with its prerequisites; the total recurring cost presented the way the client will experience it - per period, all in, including delivery and any equipment charge - and the exit terms. One page of arithmetic a controller can check beats a glossy brochure every time, and anything you cannot substantiate simply does not go in. The proposal is also where the honest sizing and the displacement comparison become visible commitments rather than sales talk.

included: all-in recurring cost presentation and exit terms
excluded: internal margin and cost-to-serve arithmetic
installation scheduling detail and route insertion
claims or comparisons whose source cannot be produced

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: win and loss notes showing which proposal elements decided the outcome

pros.claim: Stating the consumption assumption in the proposal makes the later true-up a planned event rather than an argument
pros.example: a proposal whose front page names the assumed daily cups and the review date at which quantities change

cons.claim: A fully transparent proposal invites line-by-line negotiation that a bundled price avoids
cons.example: a controller who wants the delivery component itemised and then challenged separately

failure_modes: presenting a single confident consumption number instead of the band that was actually estimated
quoting product categories rather than the specific items and formats the account will receive
omitting the exit terms until the agreement is in front of the signer
promising a cadence the route cannot actually hold
acceptance_tests: the proposal shows the consumption assumption, the all-in recurring cost, the equipment obligation, the cadence commitment and the exit terms on the document the client keeps
every comparison or claim in the proposal can be traced to a client record or the operator's own quoted price
revisit_triggers: the same proposal element is repeatedly queried or negotiated across prospects
the route's committed cadence changes
product formats or the equipment offer change

nodes.definition: Run the tasting or free trial as a structured acquisition instrument rather than a giveaway. Two forms do most of the work: a short in-office tasting where people compare what they drink now against what you would place, which resolves the blend argument before it can become a service complaint; and a time-boxed placement of the machine with product at your cost, which lets the office feel the convenience and quietly changes the default, because a machine already on the counter is much harder to remove than to keep. The play works because coffee is an experience good that nobody buys from a price sheet. It is designed with a defined duration, a named breakroom champion who will gather reactions, a stated decision date in the diary, and a pre-agreed answer to what happens on the last day - and it is never used as a way to skip qualification.

included: named champion and diarised decision date
excluded: the arithmetic of whether the trial is worth running
the written terms document itself
servicing and cleaning the trial machine on route

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged trial outcomes by segment and format from the operator's own trial history

pros.claim: A tasting settles blend preference before it becomes a recurring complaint about the coffee
pros.example: an office that chooses a darker roast in the tasting and never raises the product again

pros.claim: A machine on the counter shifts the default, so the decision becomes whether to give it up rather than whether to try something new
pros.example: an office that had planned to compare vendors and simply keeps the unit it has been using

cons.claim: Trials attract free-riders who take the placement, drink the product and never intended to sign
cons.example: an office that asks for a second extension while shopping your proposal to a competitor

failure_modes: placing a trial without a champion, so nobody inside the account owns the decision
letting the decision date pass unmarked while the equipment sits out of inventory
using the trial to bypass the qualification gate for an account that failed it
trialling a configuration you could not actually deliver at proposal price
acceptance_tests: every trial has a named champion, a written duration and a decision date recorded in the operator's own diary before the equipment leaves
the trial configuration matches what the proposal would deliver, including product format
revisit_triggers: trials in a segment stop converting
equipment inventory tightens so trials must be rationed
a trial passes its decision date without a decision

nodes.definition: Decide whether a trial is worth running by making its cost explicit as a mechanism rather than treating it as marketing. The components are concrete: the equipment is out of inventory and unavailable to another prospect for the whole trial window; the product consumed during the trial is yours; every visit to deliver, check in, retrieve or convert costs route time you could have sold; and the conversion probability for this class of prospect multiplies over all of it. The payback question is whether the expected gross margin from a converted account over a realistic account life covers the fully loaded cost of a trial divided by the conversion rate - computed with your own cost of time, your own product margins and your own observed conversion history. Which is why the first thing this node demands is discipline you may not yet have: log every trial with its equipment days, product consumed, visits made and outcome, because without that log the conversion rate is a feeling and this arithmetic is theatre.

included: conversion rate as data the operator must collect
payback framing against expected account life
excluded: any published or assumed conversion benchmark presented as fact
stop-level profitability of the converted account
equipment depreciation accounting policy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a full season of logged trial outcomes giving a conversion rate computed from the operator's own records

pros.claim: Tracking cost per conversion turns an intuition into a decision rule and ends the habit of trialling everyone who asks
pros.example: discovering after a dozen logged trials that one segment converts at a small fraction of another's rate

cons.claim: Until enough trials are logged the conversion rate is too noisy to decide on, so early decisions still rest on judgement
cons.example: the first handful of trials, where a single unreturned machine dominates the average

cons.claim: Loading every cost into the trial can make a play look unaffordable that is actually the operator's best channel
cons.example: charging full route time to a check-in visit made on a stop the van was passing anyway

failure_modes: treating trial product and equipment days as free because no invoice is raised
quoting a conversion rate from an outside source instead of measuring your own
ignoring the opportunity cost of equipment idle in an undecided trial
acceptance_tests: every trial is logged with equipment days, product consumed, visits made and outcome so a conversion rate can be computed from the operator's own history
the decision to place a trial names the expected account life and the margin mechanism that would repay the trial cost
revisit_triggers: the logged conversion rate shifts materially for a segment or format
equipment or product costs change enough to alter the payback
trial visits are being absorbed into route stops rather than costed

nodes.definition: Put the trial in writing before the machine goes on the counter, in language an office manager can read in two minutes: the duration and the end date; who owns the equipment and how and when it comes back; who pays for product consumed if the office does not convert; what happens if the unit is damaged or the suite is vacated; that no billing and no service agreement begins automatically, only on an affirmative signature; and the single decision the office is being asked to make on the decision date. The retrieval visit is scheduled at the moment of placement, not negotiated afterwards. A trial that ends with an unexpected invoice or a machine nobody will release is worse than no trial at all, because it costs the equipment, the goodwill and the referral network inside that entire building.

included: explicit no-automatic-billing and affirmative opt-in rule
excluded: drafting or interpreting the client's contractual position
the service agreement that follows conversion
collections practice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: trial outcomes showing disputes, unrecovered equipment or surprise invoices at the end of a window

pros.claim: A two-minute written trial term sheet with a scheduled retrieval date prevents almost every trial dispute before it starts
pros.example: a retrieval already in the route diary when an office decides not to convert, so the machine returns without a negotiation

cons.claim: Asking for a signature on a trial document adds friction to what the prospect thought was a casual favour
cons.example: an office manager who hesitates because anything requiring a signature must now go to their director

failure_modes: converting a trial into billing without an affirmative decision from the client
leaving retrieval to be arranged later, after which the machine becomes very hard to recover
leaving product responsibility unstated so a non-converting office receives a surprise invoice
acceptance_tests: a signed trial document states the end date, equipment ownership and retrieval, product responsibility, and that billing begins only on an affirmative signature
the retrieval visit is on the route diary from the day the equipment is placed
revisit_triggers: a trial ends in a dispute or an unrecovered machine
trial durations routinely need extending, suggesting the standard window is wrong

nodes.definition: Be able to explain in plain language, before a signature is requested, the classes of term that appear in office coffee and water service agreements: the initial term and what happens at its end, including evergreen automatic renewal versus month-to-month continuation; minimum purchase or minimum-billing clauses; equipment ownership, return, removal and refurbishment cost clauses; price-change, surcharge and fuel or delivery adjustment clauses; the service commitment and what the client is entitled to when it is missed; and assignment on a change of ownership on either side. The operator's obligation here is comprehension and disclosure, not drafting - the agreement itself is prepared and reviewed by qualified counsel, term classes and their treatment vary by jurisdiction, and the prospect should be told plainly to have their own advisor read it. Nothing in this node is legal advice, and no claim is made here about whether any clause is enforceable anywhere.

included: term classes and their plain-language explanation
the duty to point the prospect to their own advisor
excluded: drafting, amending or interpreting a specific agreement
any statement about enforceability in a jurisdiction
legal advice to the operator or the client

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: counsel review of the agreement template or a client dispute centred on a term class

pros.claim: An operator who can explain renewal and removal terms without reading from the page earns the trust that closes recurring-service deals
pros.example: answering a controller's question about what happens at the end of the initial term without hedging

cons.claim: Explaining terms honestly slows some closes and occasionally sends a prospect to their advisor and back with amendments
cons.example: a client whose counsel strikes an automatic renewal clause the operator preferred to keep

failure_modes: using an agreement template the operator has never had reviewed and cannot explain
glossing over automatic renewal or removal cost because the prospect did not ask
answering a client's legal question directly instead of directing them to their own advisor
acceptance_tests: the operator can state each term class in the agreement in plain language, and the prospect is told in writing to have their own advisor review it before signing
the agreement in use has been prepared or reviewed by qualified counsel for the operator's jurisdiction
revisit_triggers: the agreement template changes
a client's advisor raises a clause the operator could not explain
the operator begins selling in another jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Answer the four objections that carry almost every office coffee loss without lying and without scaring anyone. To we already buy it ourselves, respond with the client's own hidden costs surfaced in the displacement comparison, and concede openly when their arithmetic wins. To our landlord provides it, map what the building actually supplies, whether the suite may have its own equipment, and whether the shared breakroom is even on the tenant's floor. To we tried a service and they were unreliable, refuse to disparage the competitor and instead state your cadence commitment concretely, what you do when you miss it, and offer a reference from a stop in the same building or corridor. To it is not in the budget, offer a smaller honest configuration - fewer items, a lighter machine, a longer interval - rather than a discount that quietly destroys the stop's economics and sets up a repricing fight later. The rule over all four: never create fear about water quality, hygiene or staff retention to close.

included: evidence-based responses to the four common objections
reference and cadence commitment as the reliability answer
excluded: disparaging competitors or making unevidenced claims about their service
fear-based water, hygiene or morale arguments
discounting below the economics established at the qualification gate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: loss reasons recorded across a season showing which objection actually decided the outcome

pros.claim: Offering a smaller honest configuration instead of a discount protects the stop's economics and often closes the account anyway
pros.example: dropping to a single product line and a longer service interval for a budget-constrained nonprofit

cons.claim: Refusing to disparage a failing incumbent leaves the strongest emotional argument on the table
cons.example: declining to comment on a competitor's missed deliveries the client is already complaining about

failure_modes: discounting to win and then discovering the stop cannot pay for its own service time
escalating a water or hygiene worry into a fear argument because it is working
arguing with a client whose own numbers genuinely favour self-serve buying
acceptance_tests: each objection response used in the field is traceable to client-supplied evidence, an operational commitment the route can hold, or an honest concession
no response makes a health, safety or contamination claim the operator cannot support
revisit_triggers: the same objection repeatedly ends deals in one segment
a discount granted in the field breaches the economics the gate assumed

nodes.definition: Run acquisition as something countable rather than as a mood. The counts that matter in this trade are specific: qualified prospects per cluster, site visits completed this period, trials live right now with the decision date of each, proposals outstanding and how old they are, and new stops actually opened. The forecast of new stops is a mechanism - qualified prospects multiplied by your own observed visit-to-proposal and proposal-to-close rates, staged by how long each step really takes in your market - and its purpose is to tell you whether the top of the funnel is wide enough to reach the route density the territory needs, not to produce a number that looks good. It is also the control that stops equipment sitting on counters in trials nobody is deciding, since every live trial appears here with its date.

included: live trial register with decision dates
stop forecast from the operator's own step rates
excluded: revenue forecasting for existing accounts and route-level profitability
commission or compensation design
counting unqualified rows as pipeline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a season of measured stage-to-stage conversion from the operator's own pipeline records

pros.claim: A live trial register with dates prevents machines from sitting on counters with no decision owner
pros.example: three units out on trial that all quietly passed their decision date while the operator prospected elsewhere

cons.claim: Pipeline metrics invite vanity counting of prospects that were never gate-screened
cons.example: a list of a hundred suites presented as pipeline when only a handful have had a site visit

failure_modes: counting rows instead of qualified prospects
forecasting with rates borrowed from an outside source rather than measured from the operator's own outcomes
letting proposals age unworked because nothing tracks their date
acceptance_tests: every count in the pipeline is defined by a stage a prospect has demonstrably reached, and every live trial appears with its decision date
revisit_triggers: a cluster's forecast falls short of the density the territory needs
step rates measured this season differ materially from those used in the forecast

nodes.definition: Assemble everything the placement and route side needs the moment an account signs, so that nothing has to be rediscovered on install day. The packet carries the verified headcount and the consumption band with its stated assumptions; the agreed equipment model and water option with every prerequisite and any landlord consent in writing; the site facts from the audit sheet (counter run, outlet positions, storage location, water access, elevator and dock, delivery hours, badge or escort rules); the agreed product list, formats and opening quantities with the scheduled review date; the service cadence that was committed in the proposal; the billing contact and any vendor-portal or insurance-certificate condition still outstanding; and the champion's name with an alternate contact. This packet is the boundary of this KB: everything after it - which brewer, how it is installed and plumbed, what the par levels become, how the stop is inserted into a route - belongs to placement and logistics.

included: verified site, access and contact facts
consumption band with assumptions and review date
agreed equipment, water option and consents
excluded: equipment specification and installation work
par-level and inventory design
route insertion and scheduling
post-install service and retention activity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: install-day and first-cycle incident notes from the placement side naming what the packet failed to carry

pros.claim: A complete packet removes the install-day surprises that make a brand-new account's first impression a failure
pros.example: arriving with the right unit, the right consent letter and a booked freight elevator instead of discovering all three on the day

pros.claim: Carrying the consumption assumptions forward lets the service side confirm or correct them from real draw instead of starting blind
pros.example: the route noticing in the second cycle that draw is running under the low case and triggering the scheduled review

cons.claim: Assembling a full packet delays the start date on accounts that want equipment immediately
cons.example: a client pressing for a next-day install while a landlord consent letter is still outstanding

failure_modes: handing over a signed agreement with no site facts attached
passing forward an estimate that was never checked on site as if it were verified
omitting an unmet vendor condition so the first delivery is turned away at the door
acceptance_tests: the packet contains the signed agreement, the consumption band with assumptions and review date, the audit-sheet access facts, the opening order, and any outstanding vendor condition with an owner
no field in the packet is an estimate that was never verified on site, and unverified fields are labelled as such
revisit_triggers: an install-day problem traces back to a field the packet did not carry
the account changes suite, contact or access rules before installation

edges.why_related: offices are segmented only inside the clusters the territory has already fixed, so segmentation effort is never spent on corridors you will not serve
the list is ordered by cluster and then by segment, so segment definitions must exist before rows can be ranked
who holds the breakroom budget follows from tenancy and firm type, which are segment facts
outreach walks the cluster-ordered list; without it contact becomes a scattered drive
the sequence targets the mapped pain-holder and confirms the budget-holder rather than pitching whoever is at the front desk
the breakroom walk happens only by invitation, which the outreach sequence exists to earn
the current supply mode is read from what is on the counter, in the bins and in the storage closet during the visit
every factor in the consumption chain is sourced from the dated audit sheet the visit produces
feasibility rests on observed water access, drainage, floor space and the delivery path recorded on site
the comparison structure differs entirely depending on whether the status quo is club-store buying, a competitor agreement or a landlord-supplied breakroom
the comparison must be run at the volume the account will actually consume, or both sides of it are meaningless
the gate screens the low case of the band, so the band must exist before any go or no-go is possible
only a qualified account earns a hardware commitment, and the gate's low case decides which commercial model is even sound
opening quantities and any minimum are set from the band's low case, which this node produces
a trial commits equipment and product, so it is only offered to an account that has already passed the gate
the cost components being counted are exactly the equipment days, product and visits the play consumes
the written terms describe the specific play being run, its duration and its decision date
the proposal must state the equipment model and exactly what it obligates, which this node decides
the quantities, variety and review date written into the proposal come from the honest sizing rule
only water options the site verdict marks feasible may appear in the document, with their conditions attached
the terms walked with the client are the terms attached to the proposal that was presented
objections are answered against what the proposal actually says, including its cadence commitment and its cost presentation
the signed agreement and the terms the client accepted are the spine of the packet handed to placement
the pipeline counts qualified prospects, and only the gate defines what qualified means
first contact must identify the operator and the purpose and must respect an opt-out permanently, which bounds every contact tactic available
edges.benefit_of_coupling: prospects who are told plainly who is calling and why are far less likely to treat the whole trade as nuisance selling

edges.why_related: whichever model is chosen, how the hardware is paid for must be said out loud, which forbids describing placed equipment as free
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a client who understands the recovery mechanism does not experience product pricing as a hidden charge later

edges.why_related: the no-automatic-billing and affirmative-opt-in rules in the trial document are the conduct standard applied to trials
edges.benefit_of_coupling: no trial can quietly become a billed agreement, which is the single most damaging failure mode of the trial play

edges.why_related: the prohibition on fear-based water, hygiene and morale claims removes the most tempting answers to a wavering prospect
edges.benefit_of_coupling: objection handling stays inside claims the operator can substantiate, which protects both the client and the operator

edges.why_related: plumbing, cross-connection and potable-water obligation classes bound which water options may even be offered at a site
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the feasibility verdict inherits the verify-locally discipline instead of assuming a connection is permitted

edges.why_related: unmet vendor conditions such as an insurance certificate, badging or portal onboarding must travel with the account or the first delivery is turned away
edges.benefit_of_coupling: compliance conditions become a named field with an owner rather than an install-day discovery

edges.why_related: recovering placed hardware pushes toward larger minimum commitments and wider product lists, while honest sizing pushes opening quantities down to the low case
edges.risk_of_conflict: an account signed on a minimum it cannot consume, which becomes a closet of stale product and a cancellation
edges.resolution_rule: the low case of the consumption band caps any minimum commitment; if placement cannot be recovered under that cap, switch to rental or purchase rather than inflating what the client must buy

edges.why_related: the trial is the most persuasive tool available and therefore the strongest temptation to skip qualification for an account that failed the low-case screen
edges.risk_of_conflict: hardware financed into a stop whose consumables can never repay the service time it consumes
edges.resolution_rule: the gate is applied before any equipment leaves inventory; a trial may never be used to qualify an account that failed the low case, except under a recorded density exception in a building already served
