edges.why_related: the most persuasive version of the displacement case is always the one with unverifiable hidden costs and a hint of hygiene worry attached
edges.risk_of_conflict: a savings claim that collapses under a controller's review and takes the operator's credibility with it
edges.resolution_rule: any comparison line the client cannot verify from their own records is struck from the case, and no hygiene or water-quality framing is used as a closing device; disclosure conduct dominates persuasive framing without exception

edges.why_related: the supply mode diagnosed on site determines which of the four objections you will actually face and which evidence answers it
edges.example: a landlord-supplied breakroom always produces the permission objection rather than the price objection

edges.why_related: product preferences and observed draw captured during the tasting or trial directly determine the item list and quantities the proposal specifies
edges.example: a two-week placement whose measured draw replaces an estimated factor in the proposal's stated assumption

edges.why_related: the gate is never run before the visit, because a decision made on directory headcount is a guess wearing a decision's clothes
the proposal is presented at the diarised trial decision date, after the terms have already set expectations for what that day decides
actual draw measured after placement is the only real test of the factor chain, and it flows back to correct capture share and cups-per-drinker for the whole segment
a cluster whose qualified pipeline cannot reach the density the route needs is evidence that the territory itself must be redrawn or extended
both are mechanism-form arithmetic assembled from real records - the client's receipts in one case, the operator's own trial log in the other - rather than from any quoted market figure

conflict_axes.name: cluster_density_vs_account_attractiveness
conflict_axes.description: The most attractive prospect is frequently the one furthest from your existing stops, and route cost accrues per visit while revenue accrues per account.
poles: take the large account wherever it sits
take only what the drive loop can absorb
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the cluster rule by default and allow only recorded density exceptions, preferring accounts inside buildings already served where marginal drive time is near zero

conflict_axes.name: confident_single_number_vs_defensible_band
conflict_axes.description: Clients want one figure for what they will consume and spend, while an honest estimate built from five uncertain factors is a range.
poles: present one confident number
present the band with its assumptions
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: present the band with its stated assumptions and commit contractually only against its low case, using the scheduled review as the mechanism that narrows it

conflict_axes.name: opening_light_vs_early_stockout
conflict_axes.description: Sizing the first order to the low case protects the client from overstocking but raises the chance of running dry in the first cycles, which is the failure a new account remembers.
poles: order conservatively and top up
order generously and avoid any early gap
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: open at the low case but shorten the interval to the first review and tell the client that an early top-up is expected rather than a failure

conflict_axes.name: placed_equipment_vs_transparent_charge
conflict_axes.description: Placement wins deals because the machine appears to cost nothing, while a stated rental charge is harder to sell but honest about where the hardware is paid for.
poles: place equipment and recover in product
charge for equipment explicitly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: either model is legitimate provided the recovery is disclosed in plain words; when the consumption band cannot support recovery, do not place

conflict_axes.name: trial_generosity_vs_equipment_capital
conflict_axes.description: Every trial ties up a machine and consumes product, so a generous trial policy competes directly with placements at accounts that have already signed.
poles: trial anyone who shows interest
ration trials against inventory and conversion history
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ration trials by the logged conversion rate for that segment and by current inventory, and enforce diarised decision dates so no unit sits idle

conflict_axes.name: speed_to_signature_vs_full_disclosure
conflict_axes.description: Walking a prospect through renewal behaviour, minimums and removal costs slows the close and occasionally loses it, while skipping that walk buys a signature and a cancellation.
poles: close while enthusiasm is high
disclose fully before signature
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure wins every time; where speed matters, shorten the document rather than the explanation, and record that the client was told to have their own advisor review it

conflict_axes.name: persuasive_contrast_vs_fair_characterisation
conflict_axes.description: The strongest emotional arguments available are attacking a failing incumbent and raising doubts about water or hygiene, and both are off limits.
poles: press the contrast hard
state only what you can evidence
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer reliability complaints with your own cadence commitment and a reference, never with a claim about the competitor, and sell water on taste and convenience rather than safety

conflict_axes.name: headcount_promise_vs_hybrid_reality
conflict_axes.description: Badge count is the number a prospect volunteers and the number that inflates every estimate, while typical on-site attendance is the number that actually drinks coffee.
poles: size to the headcount the client states
size to observed on-site attendance
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use observed attendance for the low case and the stated headcount only for the high end of the band, and revisit both after the first cycles of real draw

conflict_axes.name: prospect_volume_vs_qualification_depth
conflict_axes.description: A site visit costs an hour that could have touched ten more suites, so breadth of contact competes with the discovery depth every honest number depends on.
poles: touch as many prospects as possible
qualify deeply before proposing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep contact broad and cheap up to the point of interest, then refuse to write any number without the visit; count only visited prospects as pipeline

conflict_axes.name: water_upsell_appetite_vs_site_feasibility
conflict_axes.description: Adding a water system raises the value of a stop considerably, which is precisely why it gets promised before anyone has checked whether the building allows it.
poles: attach water to every proposal
offer only what the site verdict permits
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: no water option enters a proposal before the feasibility verdict and its conditions are recorded; where consent is pending, present it as conditional and dated

edge_cases.description: An incumbent service agreement with an automatic renewal clause surfaces after the prospect has already signed with you
edge_cases.trigger: the client believed they were free to switch and a predecessor's agreement resurfaces
edge_cases.mitigation: pause the start date and place nothing; ask the client to review their own obligations with their own advisor, never counsel or assist a breach, and hold your agreement open with a revised commencement date

edge_cases.description: A trial machine will not come back: the office neither converts nor releases the equipment
edge_cases.trigger: the decision date passes and retrieval is repeatedly deferred by the client
edge_cases.mitigation: rely on the written retrieval date agreed at placement, offer the conversion or the collection as a single choice on a stated day, and treat the loss in the trial log so the segment's economics reflect it

edge_cases.description: Headcount collapses immediately after signing through a layoff or a new remote-work policy, invalidating the consumption band
edge_cases.trigger: the account's on-site attendance drops sharply within the first cycles
edge_cases.mitigation: re-derive the band from new attendance, cut standing quantities at once rather than at the next review, and do not enforce a minimum the client can no longer consume; if the stop no longer qualifies, say so and restructure or release the account

edge_cases.description: The landlord already supplies the breakroom, or the lease forbids tenant equipment in a shared kitchen
edge_cases.trigger: a multi-tenant suite where the building controls the breakroom
edge_cases.mitigation: redirect the conversation to the property manager as a building-wide prospect, or scope an in-suite arrangement the lease permits; never install into shared space on a tenant's assurance alone

edge_cases.description: The champion who drove the whole deal leaves the company between signature and installation
edge_cases.trigger: the single internal contact departs or changes role
edge_cases.mitigation: use the recorded alternate contact, re-confirm the agreement and the opening order with whoever inherits the breakroom, and re-walk the disclosure points rather than assuming they were passed on

edge_cases.description: The client wants a plumbed point-of-use system in a suite where the lease, the building, or a local trade or permit class blocks it
edge_cases.trigger: a water upgrade is requested at a site the feasibility verdict marks conditional or infeasible
edge_cases.mitigation: offer the delivered-bottle alternative, state the conditions that would make the plumbed option possible with the verify-locally flag attached, and decline to install until written consent and the applicable trade or permit class are confirmed

edge_cases.description: A prospect asks you to match a national vendor's quote that you cannot see or verify
edge_cases.trigger: a competitive quote is described verbally with a figure attached
edge_cases.mitigation: decline to match a number you cannot examine, restate your own all-in cost and what it includes, offer a smaller honest configuration if budget is the real constraint, and walk away when a match would break the economics the gate assumed

edge_cases.description: A corporate prospect's vendor-onboarding requires insurance conditions, background checks or a portal registration the operator does not currently satisfy
edge_cases.trigger: procurement sends onboarding requirements after verbal agreement
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the requirements as a gating condition with a named owner and a date, confirm what is actually achievable with your own advisors before promising a start, and hold the installation until the conditions are met rather than delivering into a refusal at the door

edge_cases.description: A very small nonprofit or a struggling firm asks for a programme their own numbers clearly cannot support
edge_cases.trigger: an enthusiastic buyer with a budget the consumption band cannot justify
edge_cases.mitigation: offer the smallest honest configuration or advise that self-serve buying remains better for them today, place nothing with a minimum they cannot carry, and record the decline reason with a reconsideration condition

edge_cases.description: The site visit reveals a genuinely unpleasant breakroom condition, such as a filthy legacy brewer or a leaking cooler
edge_cases.trigger: observed sanitation problems in the prospect's existing setup
edge_cases.mitigation: report what was observed factually and without dramatising it into a health argument, note that remediation and cleaning cadence belong to the placement and service side, and let the client decide with the facts in front of them

edge_cases.description: Two prospects in the same building both want a trial while only one suitable machine is free
edge_cases.trigger: trial demand exceeds available equipment inventory in one cluster
edge_cases.mitigation: allocate to the prospect with the stronger low-case band and the nearer decision date, offer the other an in-office tasting instead of a placement, and record the queue so the second is not lost

edge_cases.description: A seasonal or project-driven office whose on-site headcount triples for part of the year
edge_cases.trigger: an account with a known busy season, a tax deadline, a harvest or a project crew
edge_cases.mitigation: model two bands rather than one, size the standing order to the quiet season, and agree in advance how the peak is covered by temporary uplift instead of by a year-round quantity nobody drinks in the off season

workflow.action: Draw the serviceable territory as drivable clusters
workflow.description: Identify the office-dense corridors that can each be served as one loop, count the candidate offices in each, and write the rule for out-of-cluster prospects
workflow.artifact: cluster map with counted candidate inventory and an out-of-cluster rule
workflow.gate: each cluster is drivable as a single service loop and carries a counted candidate list, and the exception rule is written down

workflow.action: Segment the offices in each cluster
workflow.description: Classify candidates by headcount band, on-site pattern, culture, tenancy and shift, recording the evidence behind each classification
workflow.artifact: segment table with evidence per prospect
workflow.gate: every candidate carries a segment and the observable facts that placed it there, with hybrid and multi-shift cases explicitly flagged

workflow.action: Screen obligation classes and vendor requirements for the territory
workflow.description: List licensing, food-handling and sanitation, potable-water, transport and client-side vendor requirement classes with the authority or party that owns each
workflow.artifact: obligation-class register with verification owners and dates
workflow.gate: every entry is a class with a verify-locally flag and a named party to confirm it; nothing is recorded as a settled requirement

workflow.description: Assemble rows from directories, signage, property managers and windshield observation, ordered by cluster then segment, each row dated
workflow.gate: each row has address with suite, a headcount estimate with its source, tenancy type and a date, and rows are grouped by cluster

workflow.action: Map decision roles and run permission-based outreach
workflow.description: Identify pain-holder, budget-holder and veto-holder including the landlord where relevant, then make identified, opt-out-respecting contact prioritising buildings already served
workflow.artifact: contact log with mapped roles and outcomes per prospect
workflow.gate: every first contact identifies operator, company and purpose; the three roles are named before any proposal; opt-outs are recorded permanently

workflow.description: Walk the breakroom and capture occupancy, current equipment and product, bin evidence, water source, storage, counter, electrical and delivery access on a dated sheet
workflow.gate: every field needed by the consumption chain and the handoff packet is filled or explicitly marked unknown

workflow.action: Diagnose the current supply mode and any existing agreement
workflow.description: Classify how the office is supplied today, capture the incumbent failure signature in the client's own words, and flag any possible existing agreement
workflow.artifact: supply-mode record with failure signature and agreement flag
workflow.gate: the supply mode is evidenced, and where an agreement may exist the client has been asked to confirm their own position before a start date is set

workflow.action: Build the consumption band from the audit sheet
workflow.description: Multiply the observed factors into a low-mid-high band, convert to product units by the intended format, and write down every assumption
workflow.artifact: consumption band with per-factor evidence and stated assumptions
workflow.gate: no factor is an assumed market average, the format conversion is named, and the low case is identified as the decision number

workflow.description: Screen the low case against the mechanism by which a stop repays its service and drive time, plus the non-economic disqualifiers, and record the decision
workflow.artifact: written go or no-go with reason and, where declined, a reconsideration condition
workflow.gate: the decision is recorded before any equipment or trial is committed, and any density exception names the building and the existing stop that justifies it

workflow.action: Decide, cost and document the tasting or trial
workflow.description: Choose the tasting or the time-boxed placement, cost it from equipment days, product and visits against your own logged conversion history, and put the terms in writing before anything leaves inventory
workflow.artifact: signed trial term sheet plus a trial log entry with a diarised decision and retrieval date
workflow.gate: a named champion, an end date, retrieval arrangements, product responsibility and an explicit no-automatic-billing statement are all in writing before the equipment moves

workflow.action: Select the equipment model and build the honestly sized proposal
workflow.description: Choose placement, rental or purchase from the band and expected account life, set opening quantities at or below the low case with a review date, attach only feasible water options, and present the all-in recurring cost, cadence commitment and exit terms
workflow.artifact: one-page checkable proposal with stated assumptions and review date
workflow.gate: the consumption assumption, all-in cost, equipment obligation and its recovery, cadence commitment and exit terms are all on the document the client keeps, and every claim traces to a client record or your own quoted price

workflow.action: Walk the terms, close, and hand the account to placement
workflow.description: Explain each term class in plain language, direct the client to their own advisor, then assemble the verified site, access, consent, product and contact facts for the placement and route side
workflow.artifact: signed agreement plus the completed handoff packet
workflow.gate: the client can restate cost, obligation and exit before signing, and the packet carries no unverified field that is not explicitly labelled as unverified

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because territory, segmentation, selling conduct and obligation classes bound every later choice: an account outside the drive loop, a claim you cannot support, or an unverified permit class invalidates the work downstream of it. Prospecting and the breakroom site visit follow, because every number this KB produces is sourced from observed evidence rather than assumed averages. Diagnosis, the consumption band and the qualification gate then decide whether an account exists at all, and only a qualified account earns trial equipment, an offer model and a proposal. Terms literacy, objection handling and the handoff packet close the sequence because they convert a decision into a serviceable stop that placement and route setup can accept without rediscovering anything.

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure and honest characterisation dominate every persuasive consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: a sale made on an undisclosed obligation or an unsupportable claim is a cancellation, a refund and a reputation problem inside a building where you sell to the neighbours
dominance_rules.trigger: any pitch, comparison, proposal or objection response
dominance_rules.action: strike any claim the operator cannot substantiate and state cost, obligation and exit terms before asking for a signature

dominance_rules.rule: The low case of the consumption band dominates the optimistic case in every commitment decision
dominance_rules.rationale: gates, minimums, opening orders and hardware placements all create obligations that only the low case can safely carry
dominance_rules.trigger: qualification, minimum-commitment sizing, opening order sizing or a placement decision
dominance_rules.action: compute the decision against the low case and record the high case only as upside

dominance_rules.rule: Site-observed evidence dominates directory data and client self-report where they disagree
dominance_rules.rationale: badge counts, listed headcounts and enthusiastic estimates are systematically higher than the number of people who are actually in the building drinking coffee
dominance_rules.trigger: a conflict between the audit sheet and any stated or listed figure
dominance_rules.action: use the observed figure for the low case and treat the stated figure as the upper bound only

dominance_rules.rationale: cost accrues per visit, so an account that cannot be served inside a drive loop destroys margin no matter how large it looks
dominance_rules.trigger: a strong prospect outside every defined cluster
dominance_rules.action: decline or waitlist it, or accept it only as a recorded density exception with the added drive time acknowledged

dominance_rules.rule: An unresolved incumbent agreement dominates a signed order
dominance_rules.rationale: placing equipment into a live competitor agreement exposes the client to a dispute the operator caused and is not the operator's decision to make
dominance_rules.trigger: any indication that an existing service agreement may still bind the prospect
dominance_rules.action: hold the start date, ask the client to confirm their own position with their own advisor, and never advise or assist a breach

dominance_rules.rule: Obligation-class verification dominates the promised start date
dominance_rules.rationale: food-handling, sanitation, potable-water and vendor-insurance conditions are not negotiable by enthusiasm, and a refused first delivery is a permanent first impression
dominance_rules.trigger: any water, food-adjacent or vendor-onboarding condition that has not been verified for this jurisdiction and this client
dominance_rules.action: move the start date rather than the requirement, and record the verification owner and date

dominance_rules.rationale: an account loaded beyond what its own numbers support becomes stale product, resentment and a cancellation, and the harm lands on a small buyer who trusted the operator's judgement
dominance_rules.trigger: the honest configuration is smaller than the one the client is willing to sign
dominance_rules.action: propose the smaller configuration, or advise self-serve buying, and record the recommendation

dominance_rules.rule: Written trial terms dominate any verbal understanding
dominance_rules.rationale: every expensive trial failure - the surprise invoice, the unreturned machine, the endless extension - traces to something that was agreed only in conversation
dominance_rules.trigger: equipment about to leave inventory for a trial
dominance_rules.action: no unit moves without a signed term sheet naming the end date, retrieval, product responsibility and the no-automatic-billing rule

dominance_rules.rule: Downstream service feasibility dominates an acquisition promise
dominance_rules.rationale: acquisition can promise a cadence in seconds that the route cannot hold for a year, and the client experiences the broken promise, not the sale
dominance_rules.trigger: the placement or route side reports that a promised cadence, install date or water option cannot be delivered
dominance_rules.action: change the promise and re-present it to the client rather than pressing the route to absorb it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Draw the clusters before building any prospect list
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scattered list that must be re-qualified and re-ordered once the route's real drive time is understood

anti_rework_rules.rule: Screen obligation classes and each segment's vendor requirements before presenting proposals
anti_rework_rules.prevents: signed accounts that stall in a procurement portal or on an insurance condition, forcing a renegotiated start date

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the site visit before writing any number the client will see
anti_rework_rules.prevents: proposals built on directory headcount that collapse at the first invoice and have to be rebuilt from scratch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the budget-holder and any landlord authority before presenting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: presenting the same proposal twice, or discovering after signature that the building controls the breakroom

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify water feasibility, consent and trade or permit classes before offering a plumbed option
anti_rework_rules.prevents: withdrawing an option already promised, which costs more credibility than never offering it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the qualification gate before any equipment leaves inventory, trials included
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hardware financed into stops that cannot repay it and later written off or retrieved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the trial end date, retrieval and product responsibility in writing before the machine ships
anti_rework_rules.prevents: trial disputes, surprise invoices and unrecoverable equipment that no later conversation resolves

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size the opening order from the low case with a scheduled review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: overstocked closets, stale product, credit notes and the early cancellation that follows them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture delivery access facts during the site visit rather than on install day
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a failed first delivery, a rebooked freight elevator and a new account whose first experience is your absence

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first service cycles of actual draw fall outside the estimated consumption band
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the factor chain from the real draw, adjust standing quantities immediately, and correct the segment's assumed capture share for future estimates

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cluster's qualified prospects are exhausted or its forecast cannot reach the density the route needs
iteration_protocol.action: redraw or extend the territory, re-segment the new corridors, and rebuild the prospect list before spending more prospecting days there

iteration_protocol.trigger: logged trials show a segment or format converting materially worse than assumed
iteration_protocol.action: retune who is offered a placement trial versus a tasting, and re-cost the play from the updated conversion history

iteration_protocol.trigger: proposals are repeatedly lost at the same objection
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the displacement comparison and the objection response for that pattern using recorded loss reasons, and adjust what the proposal states up front

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new account cancels within its first cycles
iteration_protocol.action: audit whether it was overstocked, over-promised, wrongly gated or under-disclosed, and fix the node that produced the error before signing another account in that segment

iteration_protocol.trigger: a jurisdiction, landlord or client organisation changes a requirement the register did not anticipate
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the affected obligation classes with the responsible authority or party and re-issue any feasibility verdict that depended on them

iteration_protocol.trigger: equipment inventory is tied up in trials that have passed their decision dates
iteration_protocol.action: force the decision on each open trial against its written terms, retrieve where there is no decision, and tighten trial rationing until inventory recovers

iteration_protocol.trigger: the placement or route side reports that a committed cadence, install date or water option cannot be delivered
iteration_protocol.action: correct the promise with the client in writing, adjust what future proposals may commit, and re-check whether the account still passes the gate under the revised service pattern
